channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Trump calls off strike against Iran, says a deal is close
item.description: President Trump backed away from a threatened attack on Iran again, claiming regional diplomacy has opened a path to a deal.
item.content:encoded: President Trump backed away from a threatened attack on Iran again, claiming regional diplomacy has opened a path to a deal.

item.title: Iran expert on Tehran's view as Trump says there's a pending deal
item.description: NPR's A Martínez speaks with Iran expert and analyst Karim Sadjadpour about the view from Iran as President Trump says there is potential to wind down the war.
item.content:encoded: NPR's A Martínez speaks with Iran expert and analyst Karim Sadjadpour about the view from Iran as President Trump says there is potential to wind down the war.

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: Trump calls off Iran strikes, says a deal is near; tensions between Trump and Senate GOP continue as recess approaches; Progressive candidates' primary wins spark debate on midterm electability.

item.title: Activist David Hogg talks about the future of the Democratic Party
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with gun violence prevention activist David Hogg about the future of the Democratic Party and calls for him to lead the Democratic National Committee.

item.title: Thousands evacuated as 3 fast-moving wildfires burn across eastern Washington state
item.description: Thousands of people have been evacuated from their homes, as three wildfires threaten several Spokane, Washington neighborhoods. No fatalities have been reported.
item.content:encoded: Thousands of people have been evacuated from their homes, as three wildfires threaten several Spokane, Washington neighborhoods. No fatalities have been reported.
item.dc:creator: Anna King

item.title: Spokane mayor talks about the raging wildfires in the region
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Lisa Brown, the mayor of Spokane, Washington, about wildfires that have burned hundreds of homes and businesses in and around the city.

item.title: Common advice about kid snacking is outdated. Here's what parents should know
item.description: Pediatricians recommend kids eat about five times a day: three meals and two snacks. Parents often carry snacks so kids can eat on the go. Here's what science says about snacking.
item.content:encoded: Pediatricians recommend kids eat about five times a day: three meals and two snacks. Parents often carry snacks so kids can eat on the go. Here's what science says about snacking.
item.dc:creator: Michaeleen Doucleff

item.title: Trump and Senate GOP deadlocked on key issues as congressional recess approaches
item.description: With a long congressional recess set to begin at the end of the week, Senate Republicans have a lot they want to accomplish. But they're deadlocked with President Trump on several key GOP priorities.
item.content:encoded: With a long congressional recess set to begin at the end of the week, Senate Republicans have a lot they want to accomplish. But they're deadlocked with President Trump on several key GOP priorities.

item.title: Political strategist weighs in on the tension between Trump and Senate Republicans
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with political strategist Alex Conant about the tensions between the Senate and President Trump ahead of the long congressional recess that starts later this week.

item.title: U.S. steps in to help shore up Japanese yen
item.description: The U.S. dollar weakened against the Japanese yen Monday after the leaders of both countries confirmed they intervened in the markets to help shore up Japan's currency.
